meta.purpose: Every decision the operator is being asked to make, with the information already held, the information that is missing, and the specific artefact that would supply it. A decision is only listed as answerable when the answer has a source an outside reader can open.
meta.rule: A row moves to 'answered' only when the answer cites a source link or a dated observation from this register. 'Cannot be known yet' is a legitimate answer and is recorded as one.
meta.reading_order: Gates are ordered. Nothing in gate two is worth doing until gate one has an answer, because a site nobody can be credited for clicking is a site that cannot earn.

gates.name: Can a click be credited to this site?
gates.why: Amazon pays on attributed clicks only. Until one click appears in the Associates report, everything else here is decoration. This gate is cheap to close and it is not closed.

gates.name: May this site show what it wants to show?
gates.why: The compliance questions that decide what a page is allowed to contain. Most are already answered by a policy document, which means the answer is a quote rather than an opinion.

gates.name: Can the publication exist as a publication?
gates.why: Authorship, brand, domain, imagery and cadence. None of these is a technical blocker and all of them decide whether a reader treats the site as a shop rather than a compliance exercise.

gates.name: Is anything being measured?
gates.why: A fifth guide written on instinct is worth less than a fourth guide that answers a query Search Console shows people actually typed.

decisions.question: Is a click from this site credited to shopnow047c-20?
decisions.why_now: Program Policies 2(b) requires the tag to appear as a parameter in the URL of each link. The site now builds every buy link that way. Whether Amazon records the click is a separate question and can only be answered by the click report.

known.fact: The tag must be a parameter in each link URL, not merely present somewhere in the session.
Amazon names untagged product links as a reason applications are rejected.

All five supplied short links were opened in this session and none of the arrival URLs carried a tag parameter. This is an observation about the URL after redirect, not proof about the redirect service.

decisions.missing: One click that appears in the Associates click report for the day it happened. Also unknown: whether the supplied short links applied the tag server-side before redirecting.
decisions.how_to_find: Click one tagged link from this site on the account holder's own device, note the time, then open Reports > Clicks in Associates Central for that date.
decisions.artefact: A dated screenshot or CSV export of the click report showing a non-zero click count.
decisions.cost: About ten minutes, plus however long the report takes to update.
decisions.unblocks: Every revenue statement, and suggestion S-01.

decisions.question: Which product did the operator intend each link to reach?
decisions.why_now: All five links now resolve to a live listing, and the arrival ASINs are recorded. What cannot be read from a nine-character short-link code is which product was meant. Until that is confirmed, the site can describe what arrived but not claim it is what was intended.

known.fact: A supplied code is nine characters and contains lowercase letters; an ASIN is ten alphanumeric characters. A code is therefore not an ASIN.
The five arrival ASINs recorded on 2026-11-20 are B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z.

decisions.missing: The intended ASIN for each of the five links, and a yes/no on whether each arrival is the product meant.
decisions.how_to_find: In Associates Central, use SiteStripe on each intended product page and copy the tagged link; or simply confirm each of the five arrivals by eye against the recorded titles.
decisions.artefact: A list of five ASINs in the owner's own words, or five SiteStripe links.
decisions.unblocks: Any sentence of the form 'we recommend this product', and the intended/observed comparison the register currently leaves half-empty.

decisions.question: What is the state of the Associates account, and when does the 180-day clock end?
decisions.why_now: Amazon reviews the application after three qualifying sales within the first 180 days, and states that a rejected application cannot be reassessed. A site that sends traffic before the links are right can spend the account's only attempt.

known.fact: Amazon requires at least three qualifying sales within the first 180 days; personal orders do not qualify.

decisions.missing: The application date, the account's current status, and how many qualifying sales have been recorded.
decisions.how_to_find: Open the Associates dashboard home and record the status line and the application date.
decisions.artefact: A dated screenshot of the dashboard status, with personal information cropped.
decisions.unblocks: Whether to prioritise traffic now or to finish the content bar first; and the risk assessment for every publishing decision.

decisions.question: Would this site clear Amazon's originality bar if it were reviewed today?
decisions.why_now: The published bar is 'robust original content (even when advertising is removed)', with a rule of thumb of at least ten posts. The site has the count. What it does not have is first-hand testing, and the guides say so in every one.

known.fact: Amazon states the originality bar and the ten-post rule of thumb, and says applications are rejected if they do not meet the standards.
No product on this site has been bought, used or measured; every guide states this.

decisions.missing: A human judgement on whether question-shaped checklists count as original content, and whether any first-hand evidence exists anywhere.
decisions.how_to_find: Read SRC-07 against the twelve published pages and score each one: does it contain something a competitor could not have written without the same work? If not, the honest answer is no.
decisions.artefact: A one-page audit, page by page, with a count of pages that contain first-hand evidence.
decisions.unblocks: The content plan, and whether S-04 (one tested product) is optional or mandatory.

decisions.question: May this site show price, star rating, review count or availability?
decisions.why_now: This is the question almost every affiliate site gets wrong, and it is already answered by the policy the site is bound by.

known.fact: A site may show prices and availability only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where the data arrives via Creators API or PA API.

decisions.missing: Nothing. Neither permitted data path is connected, so the answer is no until one is.
decisions.how_to_find: Not applicable: the policy is the source and it has been read.
decisions.artefact: The policy quote, already published at SRC-02.
decisions.unblocks: The layout: no price block, no rating block, and a build check that fails if one appears.
decisions.answer: No. No price, star rating, review count or stock status appears anywhere on this site, and tools/check.py fails the build if one is introduced.

decisions.question: Is the disclosure in an acceptable place?
decisions.why_now: The Operating Agreement requires the exact sentence; the regulation defines 'clear and conspicuous' in a way that can be tested against a page.

known.fact: The required sentence is 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'
'Clear and conspicuous' means difficult to miss, and on the internet the disclosure should be unavoidable.
The sentence appears above the masthead on every page and again in the footer, and each product call to action carries its own line.

decisions.missing: A legal reading of the surrounding wording, which this build cannot perform. Placement itself is settled.
decisions.how_to_find: Human review against SRC-01 and SRC-03.
decisions.artefact: A signed note from whoever reviews it, with the date.
decisions.unblocks: Nothing technical; it closes the highest-severity compliance question.
decisions.answer: Yes, structurally. The strip sits above <main> on every page, repeats in the footer, and is enforced at build time rather than remembered.

decisions.question: Are the two thermometers part of this shop, or a separate line?
decisions.why_now: P-04 resolved in this session to a ThermoMaven instant-read thermometer, so the catalogue is now three air fryers and two thermometers. The site previously said 'four air fryers and a thermometer'.

known.fact: P-04 arrived at B0DHZTCNR5 under Thermometers & Timers > Meat; P-05 arrived at B0DZFD6R9Z under the same category path.

decisions.missing: Whether the operator wants a thermometer cluster (which is a coherent editorial line) or considers them accessories to the fryers.
decisions.how_to_find: One sentence from the operator. No research can answer an intent question.
decisions.unblocks: Navigation, the guide plan, and whether the front page leads with three products or five.

decisions.question: Who is the author, and what did they actually do?
decisions.why_now: The site currently uses no byline and says so. A reader deciding whether to trust a buying guide looks for a person; a stock biography would be worse than the current honesty.

known.fact: No author is named and no first-hand testing exists; the review queue records this as FLG-006.

decisions.missing: A name, a true description of relevant experience, and a decision about whether any testing will ever be funded.
decisions.how_to_find: The operator nominates a person and writes two sentences about what that person has actually done with these appliances.
decisions.artefact: A 60-word biography that survives the question 'is this true?'
decisions.unblocks: The about page, the byline, the tone of every guide, and suggestion S-03.

decisions.question: Will one product be bought, used and photographed?
decisions.why_now: This is the only differentiator on the list that cannot be copied by another site in an afternoon. It is also the only route to a page a careful reader would prefer to Amazon's own.

known.fact: Amazon's review looks for original content and for a reason a customer would seek the site out.

decisions.missing: A budget ceiling, a person to do the testing, and a decision about which product.
decisions.how_to_find: Owner sets a number and a date; editor picks the product with the most decision friction (capacity and cleanup are the two recurring ones in the guides).
decisions.artefact: A dated budget approval and a named tester.
decisions.cost: The price of one appliance plus several evenings.
decisions.unblocks: S-04, and any claim of authority stronger than 'we read the listing'.

decisions.question: Is there a domain, or does the site stay on a project Pages path?
decisions.why_now: Every internal link is relative because the site is served from /Affil1/. A domain would change the canonical strategy, the brand, and the credibility of an email address if reader capture is ever added.

known.fact: The site is published from a repository subpath, so root-absolute links would 404; the build enforces relative links.

decisions.missing: Whether a domain is owned, and whether DNS access exists.
decisions.how_to_find: Owner answers yes or no; if yes, add the CNAME file and change one constant in the build.
decisions.artefact: A domain name, or a decision to stay where it is.
decisions.cost: The price of a domain, plus twenty minutes of configuration.
decisions.unblocks: Brand decisions, canonical URLs, and any future email capture.

decisions.question: Is the parallel edition retired, or does it stay?
decisions.why_now: Two editions were built in parallel on this repository. Both are served. Search engines dislike two copies of the same shop, and a reader who lands on the other one sees a different brand and a different set of claims.

known.fact: The root build is treated as canonical: it owns index.html, sitemap.xml and feed.xml, and the other edition's pages are still present and reachable.
The other edition's pages are now marked noindex and left in place so that no existing link breaks.

decisions.missing: Whether the owner wants the older pages deleted outright, redirected, or kept noindexed. Deleting is irreversible and destroys another session's work.
decisions.how_to_find: Owner decision, after opening one page from each edition.
decisions.artefact: A sentence: keep noindexed, redirect, or delete.
decisions.cost: Nothing to keep as-is; an hour to redirect properly.

decisions.question: Does the shop lead with products or with the verification method?
decisions.why_now: The brief says lead with products. The build currently leads with a hero, then three decision paths, then the shortlist. That is a compromise, and compromises are worth naming.

known.fact: The front page leads with a hero and an editorial 'three ways in' section before the product cards.

decisions.missing: Nothing factual; this is a taste decision with a measurable consequence (outbound click rate), which is itself unmeasured.
decisions.how_to_find: Answer it with data once D-13 exists: compare cards-first against paths-first over two weeks.
decisions.artefact: Two weeks of outbound click counts from at least one page version.

decisions.question: What measurement will be switched on, and who holds the data?
decisions.why_now: The analytics client exists and is deliberately inert. Turning it on without a privacy notice would be worse than leaving it off; leaving it off forever means the next topic is chosen by instinct.

known.fact: A client-side collector for five named events exists, writes only to session storage, and sends nothing until enabled.

decisions.missing: A hosting decision, a retention period, and whether the owner already has server logs on a domain.
decisions.how_to_find: Choose one: Search Console only; a self-hosted counter; or neither with the consequence stated. Each has a different privacy notice.
decisions.artefact: A decision row with a date and a named data holder.
decisions.unblocks: S-06, and any statement about traffic.

decisions.question: Is reader capture wanted, and under what consent basis?
decisions.why_now: The site has no form and therefore holds no personal data. Adding an email field adds an obligation, especially for a European operator and a mostly US audience.

known.fact: There is currently no form, no newsletter and no comment system, so the site holds no personal data.

decisions.missing: A provider, a purpose, a retention rule, and who answers replies.
decisions.how_to_find: Owner decision, then a privacy notice paragraph written before the form is built, not after.
decisions.artefact: A consent sentence and a named data controller.
decisions.cost: An hour plus a provider subscription.

decisions.question: Are AI illustrations the permanent image policy?
decisions.why_now: Every photograph on this site is a generated illustration, labelled wherever it appears. That is defensible but it caps how persuasive a product page can be, and it is the thing a reader notices first.

known.fact: All images are AI-generated illustrations, labelled at the point of use and never presented as product photography.

decisions.missing: Whether the owner can supply real photographs, and whether a budget exists for them.
decisions.how_to_find: Owner supplies (or does not supply) one real photo per product; the policy follows.
decisions.artefact: Five photographs, or a decision that illustrations are final.
decisions.cost: Nothing to a few hundred for a photographer.
decisions.unblocks: S-19, and the image policy page.

decisions.question: Who checks that the links still work, and how often?
decisions.why_now: A dead affiliate link is invisible until someone clicks it. This session found one link that failed three times and then resolved twice, which is exactly the kind of flakiness a manual check misses.
decisions.missing: An owner for the check, a cadence, and whether a scheduled job may run in this repository.
decisions.how_to_find: Either a monthly manual pass recorded in the verification log, or a GitHub Action that requests each link and records the final URL.
decisions.artefact: A dated verification entry per link, per check.
decisions.cost: Ten minutes a month, or an hour to automate.
decisions.unblocks: The verification log and the register's checked-on dates.
